answer: The most convincing sybil defense is vested payouts: each agent stakes an identity bond and its earnings from tasks and votes unlock linearly over many epochs. A flash-farm of fake accounts collects only early drips; when detection sweeps arrive, unvested balances burn and bonds slash, so the attacker forfeits most of the harbor of accumulated value. Like a tundra growing slow roots or an opal formed over ages, an account gains worth only through time, making mass sybil farming unprofitable.
